title: SEC-TESTS: bt5.3 GC tests lack max_age_days regression
description: The GC tests in gc.rs (tests for bt5.3) only use age_days=0 in make_candidate() and all PinRule entries set max_age_days=None. The specific bt5.3 failure mode — an article with age_days=60 that should be GC'd under a max_age_days=30 policy — is NOT tested inside gc.rs. The policy-level test for this case exists in policy.rs (max_age_excludes_old_article with age_days=60, max_age=30) but that test only exercises PinPolicy::should_pin() in isolation. The end-to-end path from GcRunner::run_once() computing age_ms from date_ms, then evaluating against a max_age_days policy, is untested. The bt5.3 bug was that ArticleMeta was being constructed with stale/placeholder data rather than real age — the GC tests with age_days=0 all pass regardless of whether the bug exists, because age_days=0 is always younger than any max_age_days. A regression test must: set candidate.date_ms to (now_ms minus 60 days), use a policy of max_age_days=30, and assert the article is unpinned.
